traits.note: FNA vol. 27, Ceratodon (McIntosh; efloras, read 2026-11-05): plants in loose to dense tufts, turfs or mats, green to yellow-green, often tinged red-brown or purple; stems (0.2-)1-3(-4) cm; leaves contorted or somewhat crisped when dry; seta red, purplish, yellow or yellow-orange, twisted when dry; capsule erect to inclined or horizontal, dark red to purplish brown. C. purpureus (same volume): leaves 0.35-2.8 mm; seta 1-3(-4) cm; capsule (1-)2-2.5(-3) mm, in subsp. purpureus inclined to horizontal, red to purplish. Wikipedia, Ceratodon purpureus (read 2026-11-05): on disturbed sites, old roofs, sidewalk cracks, burned ground; most abundant on exposed dry mineral soil; setae turn red in spring.

traits.capsule_share.note: Dioicous but fruiting freely on roofs and burned ground (Wikipedia); estimate.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Lanceolate leaves about a quarter to a third as wide as long (FNA's lanceolate).

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: Estimate for a pioneer turf on open ground; to check against Glime, Bryophyte Ecology.
